expected.name: Joan Hardy
expected.description: Joan Hardy was a young Baltimore activist and member of the Young Communist League. She attended the March 26, 1932 protest at the Japanese Embassy in Washington as a delegate from Philadelphia’s John Reed Club. Police beat her and knocked her unconscious before taking the demonstrators into custody. Her assault case was postponed to April 27. The courts later rejected the appeals of nine defendants, including Hardy, and ordered them to serve prison sentences for the antiwar demonstration.
